title: Basics of AWS Cloud Architecture
content: 6 min readNov 10, 2023--Press enter or click to view image in full sizeAWS architecture diagrams is a visual representations of the structure and components of a cloud-based system built on Amazon Web Services (AWS). If you’re new to cloud computing like me, understanding how to create these diagrams can be a game-changer.In this article, we will describe the different layers of a basic Single-Tier AWS architecture diagram, providing beginners with insights into each component and its role in building a robust cloud-based system.Why Learn Architecture DiagramsArchitecture diagrams serve as a universal language for effective communication within tech teams, enabling beginners to grasp complex cloud concepts, make informed decisions in system design, troubleshoot issues efficiently, and optimise performance.More importantly, proficiency in AWS architecture is a valuable skill sought by employers, offering beginners a strategic advantage for career growth in the dynamic tech industry. Ultimately, mastering AWS architecture lays the foundation for comprehending advanced cloud services and technologies while fostering skills in scalability, flexibility, and foundational cloud principles.Let’s quickly run through an overview of some components while building a the single tier diagram above step by stepAWS Cloud Provider: The FoundationPress enter or click to view image in full sizeAt the outer layer of our AWS architecture diagram is the AWS Cloud Provider itself. Think of it as the canvas on which we’ll paint our digital masterpiece. AWS offers a broad set of global cloud-based services, and we’re about to delve into the core elements that make up a Single-Tier architecture.2. Region: Defining Geographical ScopeWithin AWS, a region is a geographical area with multiple data centers. When setting up your architecture, you choose a region to host your resources. This decision affects latency and data residency. It’s like picking the city where you want to build your digital infrastructure.3. Virtual Private Cloud (VPC): Creating a Digital FortressThe VPC is like a private, virtual network within AWS. It allows you to isolate resources, ensuring they can communicate securely. Think of it as your digital fortress, creating a boundary for your applications and data.4. Availability Zone: Building RedundancyPress enter or click to view image in full sizeWithin a region, there are multiple Availability Zones (AZs). These are essentially separate data centers with their own power, cooling, and networking. By distributing resources across AZs, you enhance redundancy and ensure high availability, like having backup generators for your digital city.5. Public Subnet: Facing the WorldPress enter or click to view image in full sizeSubnets are like neighbourhoods in your VPC. A public subnet is like a neighbourhood with houses facing the street (the internet). It’s where you place resources that need to be directly accessible from the internet.6. EC2 Instance: The Digital WorkhorsePress enter or click to view image in full sizeAn EC2 instance is a virtual server in the cloud. It’s like a computer running in the data center, serving as the workhorse for your applications. You install your software and run your code on these instances.7. Route 53: Navigating the Digital StreetsPress enter or click to view image in full sizeRoute 53 is AWS’s managed Domain Name System (DNS) service. It’s like the street signs on the internet, translating human-readable domain names into IP addresses that computers understand. It directs traffic efficiently to your resources.8. Internet Gateway: Connecting to the Outside WorldPress enter or click to view image in full sizeThe Internet Gateway is like the gateway to your digital city. It allows communication between your VPC and the internet. Resources in public subnets use the Internet Gateway to access and be accessed by users on the internet.9. Load Balancer: Balancing the Digital LoadPress enter or click to view image in full sizeA Load Balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple EC2 instances. It’s like a traffic cop, ensuring that no single instance bears too much load. This improves fault tolerance and scalability.Get Safe’s stories in your inboxJoin Medium for free to get updates from this writer.Remember me for faster sign in10. Routing Table: Directing Traffic Within the VPCThe Routing Table is your digital GPS, directing traffic within your VPC. It specifies where the traffic should go, whether it’s heading to the internet, another subnet, or an internal resource. Think of it as the street plan for your digital city.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeBeyond the Basics: Other Essential ComponentsWhile the above components form the core of a Single-Tier architecture, there are other essential components worth exploring:Security Groups and Network ACLs: These act as digital bouncers, controlling inbound and outbound traffic to your instances and subnets.Elastic IP: Provides a static IP address for your instances, ensuring they keep the same address even if they stop and start.Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service): A scalable object storage service, acting like your digital garage for storing and retrieving any amount of data.Elastic Block Store (EBS): Offers block-level storage volumes for your EC2 instances, similar to a digital closet.Exploring Other AWS Architecture Diagrams3-Tier ArchitecturePress enter or click to view image in full sizeIn a 3-Tier architecture, we introduce additional layers:Presentation Tier (Web Layer): Involves services like Amazon S3, CloudFront, and Elastic Load Balancer to manage static content and distribute incoming web traffic.Application Tier (Logic Layer): Incorporates EC2 instances, Auto Scaling, and security groups to handle application logic and business rules.Data Tier (Database Layer): Utilizes services like Amazon RDS or DynamoDB for managing and storing application data.Serverless ArchitecturePress enter or click to view image in full sizeIn a Serverless architecture, the focus shifts from managing servers to executing individual functions:AWS Lambda: Allows you to run code without provisioning or managing servers.Amazon API Gateway: Facilitates the creation, publishing, and maintenance of APIs.AWS Step Functions: Coordinates the execution of various components of your application.Understanding AWS architecture diagrams is like learning the language of the cloud. Starting with a basic Single-Tier setup provides a solid foundation, and as you explore additional components and diverse architectures, you gain the skills to design scalable, secure, and efficient digital environments in the AWS cloud.Whether you’re envisioning a city or a metropolis in the cloud, AWS provides the tools to bring your digital aspirations to life.Note: I designed my diagram with draw.io, a fantastic tool for drawing technical plans. It’s super easy, with a drag-and-drop setup, and it’s perfect for making AWS diagrams.
